transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. To get us started, could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. Lately I keep forgetting everyday things—calls I promised to make, appointments I just wrote down, even simple errands—and it’s starting to cause problems with my husband’s care. It has just gotten very overwhelming trying to keep track of everything for him.
Did these memory lapses and feelings of being overwhelmed begin suddenly following a specific stressful event, or have they been developing gradually over a longer period of time?

The intense forgetfulness really became a major problem about a year and a quarter ago when my husband's health needs increased, but the underlying attention issues aren't entirely new. I've actually relied on strict lists to mask my distractibility my whole life, and even my grade school report cards mentioned me daydreaming and losing track of instructions. The sudden demand of managing his care simply overwhelmed the coping systems I had in place for decades.
Besides the forgetfulness and distractibility, have you been experiencing persistent low mood, loss of interest in activities, or feelings of hopelessness over the past few months?

No, I don't feel hopeless or depressed, and I haven't lost interest in my activities. I only stepped back from volunteering because I'm so afraid of making a mistake and letting people down, not because I don't want to do it anymore. Mostly, I just feel very overwhelmed and tired by all the caregiving responsibilities.
Do you find that you frequently struggle with restlessness, such as needing to fidget or having difficulty staying seated for long periods, in addition to your distractibility?

Yes, I do struggle with that. When I'm sitting in church or waiting at the clinic, I'm constantly tapping my foot, rubbing my hands, or shifting in my seat because I just can't stay still. I even find myself getting up during Bible study or appointments to straighten things up or "check on something" because sitting for too long makes me feel so antsy.
